learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial areas, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Advanced knowledge and application of a computer program for Simulation, analysis and synthesis of mechanisms.
Ability for the description, classification and kinematic and dynamic analysis of cams and gears.
Ability to kinematically calculate ordinary and epicyclic gear trains.
Knowledge and application of theorems related to the synthesis of mechanisms.
Knowledge and application of theorems related to the analysis of mechanisms.

syllabus_topics: Instantaneous center of rotation in relative or apparent motion.
Extension of kinematic analysis of mechanisms.
Extension of dynamic analysis of mechanisms.
Static and dynamic equilibrium with friction.
Transmission angle. Relationship with mechanical advantage.
Function of a cam. Displacement diagram.
Problems and improvements in the transmission of movement in cam - follower contact.
Transmission of a rotational movement between two contacting links.
Length of engagement and arc of action.
Coefficient of engagement or contact ratio.
Zero gears with straight teeth. Zero gears.
Limit number of teeth in zero gears with straight teeth.
V (shifted) gears with straight teeth. Limit number of teeth.
Corrected external toothings without variation of the center distance.
Corrected external toothings with variation of the center distance and pressure angle.
Contact ratio and contact line in helical gears
Basic kinematic design criteria for gear trains.
Kinematic design of an ordinary train.
Synthesis of mechanisms with higher kinematic pairs.
assessment_rules: The course offers progressive evaluation or a global exam for the ordinary call. For progressive evaluation, the final grade is calculated as 60% from the progressive evaluation exam, 30% from two partial tests, and 10% from lab practices. For the global ordinary exam, the final grade is 60% from Block A, 30% from Block B, and 10% from lab practices. In the extraordinary call, the final grade is solely based on a single final exam. In all cases, a minimum of 5 points is required to pass, with mandatory attendance to 3 lab sessions and a minimum of 4 points in Block A for ordinary calls.
